policy: Instructional diagrams explain generic mechanisms. They are not scale drawings, CFD/FEA results, mould designs, safety drawings, machine-specific setup instructions or production limits.

diagrams.title: Velocity to pressure transfer
diagrams.alt: Conceptual graph showing screw-position/fill progression and cavity-pressure response around velocity-to-pressure transfer.
diagrams.caption: Transfer is a process transition, not a universal screw-position number. Interpret commanded state together with actual machine response and cavity evidence.

diagrams.title: Cavity pressure through the moulding cycle
diagrams.alt: Conceptual cavity-pressure trace labelled fill, pack or hold influence, gate isolation and pressure decay.
diagrams.caption: Peak pressure alone can hide important process-history differences; location, calibration and the full trace remain part of the evidence.

diagrams.title: Feed-system pressure-loss locations
diagrams.alt: Conceptual melt path from nozzle through sprue, runner and gate into the cavity.
diagrams.caption: Separate pressure demand by flow-path region rather than assuming the smallest feature is automatically the root cause.

diagrams.title: Cooling circuit balance
diagrams.alt: Conceptual mould cooling circuit showing inlet and outlet evidence around an asymmetric hotter region.
diagrams.caption: Controller setpoints do not prove equal local thermal state. Compare flow, supply/return temperature, pressure drop and cavity-side evidence.

diagrams.title: Fountain flow and frozen-layer development
diagrams.alt: Conceptual cavity cross-section showing a hotter flowing core turning outward at the advancing flow front while cooler wall layers develop.
diagrams.caption: The diagram explains the mechanism only; actual layer thickness, orientation and thermal history depend on material, geometry and mould conditions.

diagrams.title: Gate-seal response study
diagrams.alt: Conceptual measured response versus hold-duration curve approaching a plateau.
diagrams.caption: A plateau can be useful evidence for the studied system, but it is not a universal hold-time prescription.

diagrams.title: Multi-cavity balance
diagrams.alt: Four-cavity layout fed from a common runner, illustrating why each cavity should retain its own identity.
diagrams.caption: Cavity-specific traces and quality results should be preserved before pooling; averages can hide systematic cavity offsets.

diagrams.title: Draft and ejection evidence
diagrams.alt: Conceptual moulded wall showing draft and an ejector-force direction.
diagrams.caption: Use ejector force/current, part temperature, surface condition and damage together; a rising ejector signal does not by itself prove inadequate draft.

diagrams.title: Injection moulding cycle timeline
diagrams.alt: Conceptual timeline of plasticising, filling, transfer, packing, cooling and ejection.
diagrams.caption: Each stage hands conditions to the next; durations and overlap remain machine, mould, material and process dependent.

diagrams.title: Plasticising and shot preparation
diagrams.alt: Conceptual reciprocating-screw sequence showing feed, rotation/recovery, shot preparation and forward injection.
diagrams.caption: The sequence explains function, not screw geometry, residence limits or a machine-specific setup.

diagrams.title: Thermal gradient through a moulded wall
diagrams.alt: Conceptual wall cross-section showing cooler wall-adjacent regions and a hotter core.
diagrams.caption: Actual temperature fields depend on material, wall thickness, mould construction and process conditions.

diagrams.title: Uniform shrinkage versus differential warpage
diagrams.alt: Conceptual comparison of more uniform contraction with differential deformation.
diagrams.caption: Warpage can combine shrinkage, orientation, thermal imbalance and constraint; the drawing does not assign one universal cause.

diagrams.title: Weld-line formation around an obstacle
diagrams.alt: Conceptual split flow around an obstacle followed by flow-front reunion.
diagrams.caption: Interface quality depends on local material, thermal, flow, gas and geometry conditions; no universal process adjustment is implied.

diagrams.title: Conceptual fibre-orientation layers
diagrams.alt: Conceptual reinforced-wall section showing differing local fibre directions.
diagrams.caption: The figure explains anisotropy only; it is not a quantitative orientation prediction.

diagrams.title: Specification, process distribution and capability
diagrams.alt: Conceptual process distribution between lower and upper specification limits.
diagrams.caption: Capability indices require a defined stable population and credible measurement; the curve is illustrative only.

diagrams.title: DOE interaction concept
diagrams.alt: Conceptual non-parallel response lines showing an interaction.
diagrams.caption: The figure illustrates interaction logic; it does not replace a designed, replicated and confirmed experiment.

diagrams.title: Hypothesis-driven diagnostic tree
diagrams.alt: Conceptual troubleshooting path from a defined symptom through competing mechanisms to discriminating evidence.
diagrams.caption: The tree structures reasoning; it does not prescribe unsafe tests or guarantee root cause.

diagrams.title: Dimensional change with conditioning time
diagrams.alt: Conceptual dimension-versus-time response approaching a more stable conditioning state.
diagrams.caption: Measurement timing, temperature, humidity, material and product requirements remain part of the result.

diagrams.title: Machine, mould and safety system overview
diagrams.alt: Conceptual flow from material feed through the injection unit, mould and ejection, with cooling and a distinct guarded intervention boundary.
diagrams.caption: Use the diagram to orient functions and evidence paths; actual architecture, guarding, isolation and access remain machine-, mould- and site-specific.

diagrams.title: Viscosity response to shear rate and temperature
diagrams.alt: Conceptual downward-sloping apparent-viscosity curves versus shear rate, with a higher-temperature curve shown at lower resistance.
diagrams.caption: The curves illustrate shear-thinning and temperature sensitivity only; they contain no grade-specific values or universal processing settings.

diagrams.title: Complex diagnostics evidence ledger
diagrams.alt: Conceptual evidence ledger linking one observed symptom to three competing hypotheses, predictions, discriminating tests, contradictions and updated confidence.
diagrams.caption: The ledger supports disciplined reasoning and visible uncertainty; it does not authorize unsafe tests or turn correlation into root-cause proof.
